summary: Multiple lines of evidence indicate that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalizations in patients with HFpEF. A large meta-analysis of six RCTs found SGLT2i significantly reduced the risk of heart failure hospitalizations over ≥1 year follow-up [2]. The DELIVER trial specifically showed dapagliflozin reduced worsening heart failure (defined as unplanned HF hospitalization or urgent HF visit) by 18% compared to placebo in patients with LVEF >40% [3]. A nationwide cohort study of veterans with type 2 diabetes and HFpEF found SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with reduced risk of hospital admission for heart failure [7]. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 RCTs in HFpEF patients confirmed SGLT2Is reduce hospitalization for heart failure [8]. These findings are consistent across RCTs, meta-analyses, and real-world data.
evidence_gaps: The evidence primarily focuses on patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes; less is known about SGLT2i effects on hospitalization in HFpEF patients without diabetes. Long-term data beyond 2-3 years of follow-up are limited, and most trials excluded patients with very advanced renal dysfunction or recent acute HF decompensation.
